headline: Malaysia's energy regulator warns that data centre demand is straining power supply and grid capacity.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered to 4: the remarks were made at a seminar last week, before 7 Oct 2026, so the item is stale; the article was read in full.
importance_line: It matters to Malaysian households and businesses who share a grid that data centres are straining, and to the operators, because the regulator says recovering grid investment is at risk when data centres commit to only 5 to 15 years of demand.
summary: W.Media reports that Siti Safinah Salleh, chief executive of Malaysia's Energy Commission, reportedly said at a seminar last week that data centres are pushing electricity demand growth to about 10 per cent, up from 1.5 to 2 per cent before. She warned that data centres commit to only 5 to 15 years of demand, while grid investment takes about 20 years to recover.
